title: Two places on a turntable
hook: Change distance from the axle and predict tangential speed.
misconception: tangential speed stays fixed when distance from the axle doubles.
objective: Apply v = ωr to compare tangential speed when distance from the axle changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a rigid turntable with fixed angular speed, v = ωr. When distance from the axle doubles, tangential speed becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v = ωr; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a rigid turntable with fixed angular speed, with a nonzero initial result. If distance from the axle triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on tangential speed?
recall.why: Apply v = ωr under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
